steps.text: The CLI calls load_rows(), validates required columns and pattern IDs, and hashes source bytes.
render() builds the manual; --check compares exact output and exits with an error on drift, while ordinary invocation writes CODEBOOK.md.
The normalise CLI requires configuration/output paths. build() loads configuration against its schema and checks the configured source checksum, headers, values, namespace, and ID uniqueness.

Source rows produce patterns, units, invented examples, shared rules, and preserved candidate cells. Only configured relation decisions produce typed relations; unresolved semantics are reported rather than inferred.

The output mapping includes original source bytes, hashes, and counts. persist() rejects unsafe/unowned destinations and unexpected files; writes replace generated files, while --check compares all expected bytes without writing.

flows.name: Private annotation bundle to conformance report

steps.text: The validator rebuilds expected extraction in memory and requires an exact matching catalogue before reading the input bundle; stale data is rejected.
The local schema rejects malformed structure and unknown fields. Python checks source/schema/pattern versions and work, unit, reviewer, evidence, and adjudication references.

Absence requires scope/adequacy inspection evidence. Present STR05/06/07/09/10 annotations receive configured evidence checks; event references/order and knowledge maps are checked. Uncertain/absent decisions do not have to invent a positive chain.
The CLI emits versions, source checksum, actual supplied counts, errors with paths/codes, and a scope warning. Exit 0 means conformance; it does not verify the truth of the evidence or run a pilot.
